articles.title: FATO OU FAKE: Debate Globo com candidatos ao Governo de MG no 1º turno | G1
articles.standfirst: Participaram do debate desta terça-feira (29) Alexandre Kalil (PDT), Cleitinho Azevedo (Republicanos), Flávio Roscoe (PL), Gabriel Azevedo (MDB), Mateus Simões (PSD), Patrus Ananias (PT).
articles.summary: Participaram do debate Alexandre Kalil (PDT), Cleitinho Azevedo (Republicanos), Flávio Roscoe (PL), Gabriel Azevedo (MDB), Mateus Simões (PSD), Patrus Ananias (PT).
articles.body:
Os candidatos Gabriel Azevedo (MDB), Alexandre Kalil (PDT), Patrus Ananias (PT), Cleitinho Azevedo (Republicanos), Flávio Roscoe (PL) e Mateus Simões (PSD) no estúdio da TV Globo em Minas para participar do debate entre candidatos ao governo de Minas Gerais — Foto: Douglas Magno/Globo

A Globo promoveu, nesta terça-feira (29), um debate com candidatos ao Governo de Minas Gerais. Com mediação da jornalista Liliana Junger, o encontro, realizado na redação da TV Globo em Belo Horizonte, foi transmitido ao vivo pela emissora e pelo g1 .

Os participantes, em ordem alfabética, foram:

A equipe do Fato ou Fake checou as principais declarações dos candidatos. Leia:

"Deixei R$ 500 milhões em caixa [na Prefeitura de Belo Horizonte]."

O último Demonstrativo da Disponibilidade de Caixa e Restos a Pagar da Prefeitura de Belo Horizonte, na gestão Kalil, é o de 31 de dezembro de 2021. Segundo o documento, havia cerca de de R$ 698 milhões em caixa líquido de recursos livres. Esse é o dinheiro que "sobra" depois do desconto de despesas já contratadas e que pode ser usado em qualquer área.

Kalil deixou a Prefeitura de Belo Horizonte em 25 de março de 2022 para disputar o Governo de Minas. O vice Fuad Noman assumiu o cargo .

No fim de 2022, já com Fuad Noman no cargo em nove dos doze meses do ano, o caixa líquido de recursos livres estava em R$ 722,8 milhões, perto do valor do ano anterior.

Os números oficiais antes e depois da saída de Kalil ficam acima dos R$ 500 milhões que ele citou no debate.

Procurada pelo Fato ou Fake , a assessoria de Alexandre Kalil disse, por telefone, que "o candidato fez uma aproximação do número de R$ 689 milhões, tendo já mencionado, em outras entrevistas, que o valor foi acima de R$ 600 milhões".

"A gente [Minas Gerais] é o segundo estado que mais exporta no Brasil."

Dados no Comex Stat, sistema oficial do Ministério do Desenvolvimento, Indústria, Comércio e Serviços (MDIC), mostram que Minas Gerais ocupou a 2ª posição no ranking nacional de exportações em agosto de 2026, ficando atrás somente de São Paulo.

Em terceiro lugar, ficou o Rio de Janeiro.

“Sul de Minas hoje, para você entender: as estradas são todas privatizadas, com valor de tarifa até de R$ 15.”

Nos últimos anos, o governo estadual e o governo federal realizaram leilões e repassaram alguns trechos na região à iniciativa privada. É o caso do lote de rodovias administrado pela concessionária EPR Sul de Minas, que, desde 2033, opera cerca de 454 km de malha rodoviária em municípios como Pouso Alegre, Poços de Caldas, Itajubá, Jacutinga, Ouro Fino, Monte Sião, Bueno Brandão, Andradas e Gonçalves. Entre as rodovias nessa situação, estão a MG-290, MG-173, MG-179, MG-295, MG-459, MG-455, LMG-877 e CMG-146, além de um trecho da BR-459.

A concessão, porém, abrange uma parte da rede viária do Sul de Minas. Há rodovias estaduais que contiuam sob administração direta do Departamento de Estradas de Rodagem de Minas Gerais (DER-MG), rodovias federais não concedidas sob responsabilidade do Departamento Nacional de Infraestrutura de Transportes (DNIT) e estradas vicinais, que em geral são municipais e têm manutenção a cargo das prefeituras.

Procurado pelo Fato ou Fake, o DER-MG disse, por e-mail, que: “Atualmente, estão sob a responsabilidade do DER, por meio das Unidades Regionais de Varginha, Poços de Caldas e Itajubá, 1.528,2 km de rodovias, entre trechos pavimentados e não pavimentados. Em relação à malha estadual concedida, no âmbito da Artemig, o Lote Sul de Minas compreende 454,3 km de rodovias, enquanto o Lote Varginha – Furnas compreende 432,8 km, totalizando 887,1 km de rodovias pavimentadas”.

Já a assessoria de Cleitinho Azevedo disse que: "Reconhecemos que a expressão ‘as estradas são todas privatizadas’ pode ser entendida de forma literal e, nesse sentido, não significa que 100% da malha rodoviária do Sul de Minas esteja concedida à iniciativa privada".

Já o valor da tarifa de pedágio varia em relação à concessionária, praça e categoria do veículo. A EPR Vias do Café, por exemplo, cobra R$ 15,80 de carros, caminhonetes e furgões . Essa concessão administra 432,8 km de rodovias em 22 municípios do Sul de Minas.

"A cidade de Extrema, que hoje é a quinta maior arrecadação do estado."

Segundo dados da Secretaria de Estado de Fazenda (SEF-MG), a cidade de Extrema, no Sul de Minas, arrecadou R$ 2,3 bilhões de janeiro a agosto deste ano com Imposto sobre Circulação de Mercadorias e Serviços (ICMS) e outras receitas.

Esta é a quinta maior cifra entre todos os municípios mineiros no período. Extrema ficou atrás apenas de Belo Horizonte (R$ 14,7 bilhões), Betim (R$ 8,3 bilhões), Uberlândia (R$ 4,8 bilhões) e Contagem (R$ 3,7 bilhões).

"Minas Gerais é um dos quatro estados do Brasil em que o ensino integral caiu."

O 3º Relatório de Monitoramento do Programa Escola em Tempo Integral, do Ministério da Educação, aponta que só quatro estados tiveram redução nas matrículas em tempo integral das redes estaduais entre 2022 e 2025: Minas Gerais, Paraíba, Santa Catarina e Rondônia.

Minas teve a maior perda em número absoluto: 25.106 matrículas a menos, uma queda de 13%. Na Paraíba, a redução foi de 9.894; em Santa Catarina, de 7.104; e em Rondônia, de 657.

No mesmo período, 23 unidades da federação ampliaram a oferta, e o país somou 590 mil novas matrículas em tempo integral nas redes estaduais, um crescimento de 27%.

A queda em Minas se concentrou entre 2022 e 2023, com 54.183 matrículas a menos. Nos dois anos seguintes, o estado recuperou parte do que perdeu, mas ainda não voltou ao patamar de 2022.

Levando em consideração apenas o ensino médio no período de 2019 a 2026, houve aumento nas matrículas no ensino integral. Segundo a Secretaria de Estado de Educação, o ensino médio em Tempo Integral passou de 78 escolas em 2019 para 719 em 2023. Em 2026, eram 835 escolas, com 96,9 mil alunos.

"Como a gente [gestão Simões/Zema] fez com o Samu, que hoje atende o estado inteiro."

O Samu passou a ter cobertura nos 853 municípios de Minas Gerais em dezembro de 2025, durante a gestão de Romeu Zema, quando Mateus Simões era vice-governador.

A ampliação ocorreu com a implantação do serviço nas últimas 27 cidades que ainda não tinham cobertura, no Triângulo do Sul. Com isso, o governo estadual anunciou a universalização do Samu no estado.

“Minas Gerais tem hoje uma dívida de aproximadamente R$ 200 bilhões.”

De acordo com os dados mais atualizados da Secretaria de Estado de Fazenda (SEF-MG), de 31 de agosto de 2026, Minas Gerais tem uma dívida total de R$ 208,87 bilhões.

Desse montante, R$ 188,19 bilhões são devidos à União. O saldo está sendo pago por meio do Programa de Pleno Pagamento de Dívidas dos Estados (Propag).

Outros R$ 14,3 bilhões se referem a outros contratos, como com o Banco Interamericano de Desenvolvimento (BID) e o Banco Nacional de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Social (BNDES).

Os R$ 6,3 bilhões restantes correspondem a dívidas relativas a depósitos judiciais, ao Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social (INSS), ao Instituto de Previdência dos Servidores Militares do Estado de Minas Gerais (IPSM) e a outros passivos.

"Professoras e professores que em Minas hoje recebem menos do que o valor estipulado no Plano Nacional.”

O piso nacional do magistério em 2026 foi fixado em R$ 5.130,63 para uma jornada de 40 horas semanais. Na rede estadual de Minas Gerais, a carga horária do professor de educação básica é de 24 horas semanais. Por isso, o governo do estado aplica um critério de proporcionalidade e paga um vencimento básico de R$ 3.078,50 para a categoria.

O Executivo estadual justifica o pagamento proporcional com base na própria Lei Federal 11.738, que regulamenta o piso do magistério. A legislação prevê que a remuneração referente a jornadas de trabalho diferentes de 40 horas será, no mínimo, proporcionalmente correspondente ao valor do piso nacional.

No entanto, o sindicato que representa os professores da rede estadual, o Sind-UTE/MG, contesta a política salarial adotada pelo estado. A entidade reivindica a aplicação do valor integral do piso nacional.

Procurada pelo Fato ou Fake , a assessoria de Patrus disse que o candidato considerou o apenas o posicionamento do sindicato, argumentando que "o piso nacional é referência para professores com formação em nível médio, enquanto o ingresso na carreira em Minas Gerais exige curso superior".

Participaram da checagem: Larissa Cavalcante, Leonardo Milagres, Rafaela Mansur e Rodrigo Salgado .

articles.title: Marconi Perillo promete investimento no setor agropecuário  | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato do PSDB cumpriu agenda com lideranças do campo no interior de Goiás. Ele defendeu renegociação de dívidas, linhas de crédito facilitadas e recuperação de estradas.
articles.summary: Candidato do PSDB cumpriu agenda com lideranças do campo no interior de Goiás. Ele defendeu renegociação de dívidas, linhas de crédito facilitadas e recuperação de estradas.
articles.body:
O candidato ao governo de Goiás, Marconi Perillo ( PSDB ), defendeu nesta quarta-feira (30) a ampliação de investimentos estaduais no setor agropecuário e a criação de mecanismos de socorro financeiro para conter o endividamento dos produtores rurais. A proposta foi apresentada durante agenda de campanha em Jataí , no sudoeste de Goiás, onde o candidato se reuniu com representantes do agronegócio, trabalhadores e lideranças de cooperativas agrícolas.

Marconi visitou propriedades rurais e cooperativas da região e conversou com produtores sobre o impacto da alta dos custos de insumos e as perdas provocadas por oscilações climáticas recentes. Na sequência, a comitiva participou de uma caminhada pelas ruas do centro comercial do município e encerrou a programação do dia com um ato público para apoiadores.

Marconi destacou que pretende articular um programa de refinanciamento de dívidas junto a bancos públicos e ao governo federal, além de criar fundos estaduais de aval para socorrer pequenos e médios agricultores em situação de inadimplência.

O candidato ressaltou ainda que as ações para o campo precisam abranger melhorias estruturais de longo prazo, como a pavimentação e manutenção de rodovias estaduais e estradas vicinais utilizadas no escoamento de safras.

Eleições 2026: Marconi Perillo promete investimento no setor agropecuário para diminuir endividamento de produtores rurais — Foto: Reprodução/TV Anhanguera

"O produtor rural goiano é quem sustenta a nossa economia, mas muitos estão sufocados por juros altos e quebras de safra consecutivas. Nós vamos agir em três frentes imediatas: primeiro, criar um programa estadual de socorro financeiro e renegociação de dívidas com carência estendida; segundo, garantir linhas de crédito acessíveis para que ninguém pare de produzir; e terceiro, recuperar as nossas estradas", afirmou Marconi.

De acordo com Marconi, a gestão estadual também deverá firmar parcerias para ampliar a conectividade no meio rural e subsidiar tecnologias voltadas à agricultura de precisão.

articles.title: A year on, Bengaluru-Mumbai superfast train promise remains on paper
articles.summary: A year after Centre’s promise, Bengaluru–Mumbai superfast/Vande Bharat sleeper train remains unlaunched; travel still takes ~24 hours with limited services.
articles.body: BENGALURU: A year after the Centre promised a superfast train between Bengaluru and Mumbai, there is little to show on the ground. The much-awaited service remains on paper, with passengers still relying on the same limited rail options that have frustrated traders, business travellers and regular commuters for years.On Sept 27, 2025, Bengaluru South MP Tejasvi Surya announced through his X account that railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw had assured him of a superfast train connecting the two cities. Twelve months later, however, the promised train has not started.For passengers, the situation has changed little. For over three decades, Udyan Express has remained the only daily direct service between Bengaluru and Mumbai that takes roughly 24 hours to cover the journey.There was some movement in May 2026, when railways introduced a bi-weekly SMVT Bengaluru-Lokmanya Tilak Terminus Express. But the additional service did not address the central demand for a faster connection: that train too takes around 24 hours.The next assurance raised expectations further. In May, Vaishnaw told TOI a Vande Bharat sleeper service on Bengaluru-Mumbai route will be introduced in Aug. That, too, has not materialised.The railway board subsequently allocated a rake that had initially been planned for Bengaluru-Mumbai route to Northern Railway zone, leaving passengers without a launch date for the proposed service.Rail users from across Karnataka have taken to social media to question the delay. Karnataka Rail Users sarcastically marked the first anniversary of the announcement, while other passenger groups accused the Centre and South Western Railway (SWR) zone of making promises without delivering the service.Mahendra Singhi, a member of SWR’s Zonal Railway Users’ Consultative Committee in Hubballi, said the railway board should introduce a Vande Bharat on the route to provide the speed and comfort passengers have been seeking.The BJP’s Karnataka migrant outreach network has also sought an early decision. “Nearly a year has passed since the announcement, yet there has been no official communication regarding the launch date of this service. articles.title: Bombay HC stays Sachin Waze’s bail granted by special court, issues notice on NIA appeal
articles.summary: Bombay HC stays bail for ex-cop Sachin Waze in Antilia bomb scare/Mansukh Hiran case, issues notice on NIA appeal; hearing set for Oct 7.
articles.body: MUMBAI: Following two recusals, a third division bench of Bombay high court comprising Justices Girish Kulkarni and Neela Gokhale on Wednesday stayed the bail granted by a special NIA court to former police officer Sachin Waze in the five-year-old Antilia bomb scare and Mansukh Hiran murder case under anti-terror law UAPA.The Justice Kulkarni-led bench issued notice to Waze and posted the matter for hearing on Oct 7. Waze has spent 1,999 days in custody and is at the Thane central prison.On Feb 25, 2021, an explosives-laden SUV was found near Antilia. The NIA alleged Waze orchestrated the plot to extort wealthy individuals and project himself as a “super cop” after returning to the police force from a long suspension. Its case was that Waze allegedly used Hiran’s vehicle, fabricated theft proceedings, and planted gelatin sticks and a threat note in the vehicle. Hiran was allegedly murdered on March 4, 2021 because he knew of the conspiracy and could expose it. Waze was arrested later that month.When the matter originally came up on Wednesday as scheduled, it was listed before a division bench of Justices Bharti Dangre and Ashish Chavan. Justice Dangre asked if Waze was released or not as yet. Additional solicitor general Anil Singh for NIA said he was not.Justices Dangre and Chavan recused themselves from hearing the NIA appeal against the special trial court order of bail to Waze. Justice Dangre said she had already earlier -- in Sept 2024 -- recused and directed that Waze’s matter in the NIA case not be placed before a bench where she is a party. Her 2024 order was in a quashing plea filed by Waze.Justice Dangre said to the ASG, “We understand and appreciate your inconvenience” and expressed regret that the matter would now have to be placed before another bench.Justice Chavan—who was appointed as judge last year--too recused, saying he had as a lawyer appeared for CBI in a distinctly connected matter.On Tuesday, the HC division bench of Justices Sarang Kotwal and R R Bhonsale had recused itself when the ASG had mentioned the challenge and sought urgent hearing.After Wednesday’s recusal, the ASG mentioned the matter before HC Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi to have it assigned before another bench since a few other judges on other benches too, as lawyers, appeared for Central agencies in the case. The CJ assigned the mater to Justice Kulkarni’s bench.On Tuesday, special NIA court judge Chakor S Baviskar, granting bail to Waze, had held there was “absolutely nothing on record” to infer that industrialist Mukesh Ambani or his family were ever terrorized and repeatedly questioned the lack of statements taken and dubbed as “quite hypothetical” the allegation of any demand made by Waze of money from the Ambanis. The judge observed the SUV containing gelatin sticks was parked near Shikharkunj building on Carmichael Road, and not directly opposite Antilia on Altamont Road.In its appeal, NIA before HC said the bail order was “erroneous and illegal,” passed without going into detailed facts and circumstances, and is “completely misplaced both, on facts and law.”The appeal said the special NIA court “completely ignored the rigours of Section 43 D of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act while granting bail to the main accused (Waze) whose role is ‘central’ in character to the terror crime of this case.”Waze’s record is not “unblemished” as he submits, said the NIA, citing inquiries against him. The NIA said the “very substratum of the prosecution case is that, Waze after his reinstatement in police service after a long suspension, wanted to regain his clout.” Moreover, he was “under the compelling circumstances to collect Rs 100 crore per month from hoteliers and bar owners in Mumbai and territory, and in that process, he intended huge monetary gain for himself also and for that hatched a criminal conspiracy with other accused in this case and committed all the alleged offences.”To allegedly execute his conspiracy to extort money from the wealthy, Waze “required a vehicle in which he could plant some explosives, park it in front of a residence of influential and wealthy industrialist or corporate tycoon and putting him under terror extort huge amounts for himself and to meet the alleged target given to him”, the NIA added.The Nia stressed Waze was in “search of easy and wealthy prey who would succumb to threat and provide any amount to avoid fatal consequence… and he chose the Ambani family.” The special NIA court said the day-to-day business of the Ambanis did not appear to have been disturbed “even for a minute” after the incident. articles.title: Drive wrong, pay more: Karnataka mulls Rs 5,000 fine for repeat traffic offenders
articles.summary: Karnataka may raise repeat traffic fines to Rs 5,000, add penalty points and licence suspensions, ban half-helmets, integrate e-challan systems and regulate low-speed e-bikes.
articles.body: BENGALURU: The Karnataka govt is considering higher fines for one-way driving, wrongside driving, riding on footpaths, unauthorised parking, signal jumping and dangerous riding to up to Rs 5,000 for habitual offenders. At present, the basic fine for these offences is Rs 500.The govt is contemplating bringing changes to motor vehicle rules to impose higher penalties for several traffic violations. Officials said Rs 5,000 would be the upper ceiling for habitual offenders. “Fines will vary for first-time offenders and increase progressively for each additional offence,” one of them said.A key proposal discussed at a joint meeting of the transport and home departments on Wednesday, which was attended by transport minister Byrathi Suresh and home minister Priyank Kharge, was to deal with habitual offenders. Under the proposed system, motorists would accumulate negative points for traffic violations and could face suspension of their driving licences after crossing a specified limit.A senior transport department official said: “Multiple issues pertaining to easing congestion and increasing penalties for seven to eight offences were discussed at the meeting. Once we receive a formal proposal from the home department, further measures will be taken to bring changes to rules and hike penalties.”The govt is considering banning the production and sale of half-helmets over safety concerns for two-wheeler riders and pillion riders. Suresh said the govt will even take action against factories producing half-helmets, which are cheaper than ISI-marked helmets and are widely used by two-wheeler riders. However, they don’t provide adequate protection.The departments are working towards integrating the transport department’s Sarathi system with Bengaluru traffic police’s e-challan system. This would allow traffic personnel to verify driving licence details and access a motorist’s violation history while registering fresh offences.The govt is also looking at bringing low-speed battery-operated electric two-wheelers under a legal framework covering registration, applicability of traffic rules, wearing helmets and other requirements. Officials discussed measures to ensure these vehicles can be identified and their riders held accountable for traffic violations.Push for carpoolingTo reduce the number of private vehicles on Bengaluru roads, govt is also examining a state-level policy for carpooling and ride-sharing services. The proposal includes guidelines for app-based carpooling, park-and-ride facilities and promotion of shared transport.The meeting also discussed stricter action against modified silencers, shrill horns and high-intensity lights. articles.title: Quinto dia útil de outubro de 2026: veja a data do pagamento | G1
articles.standfirst: Confira quando cai o quinto dia útil de setembro de 2026 e a data limite para o pagamento do salário.
articles.summary: Confira quando cai o quinto dia útil de setembro de 2026 e a data limite para o pagamento do salário.
articles.body:
Carteira de trabalho — Foto: Geraldo Bubniak/AEN

Para quem trabalha com carteira assinada, o quinto dia útil de outubro de 2026 cai na terça-feira, dia 6 . A data é o prazo máximo para o pagamento do salário referente ao mês anterior, setembro, conforme as regras da Consolidação das Leis do Trabalho (CLT) .

Na contagem do prazo para o pagamento dos salários, o sábado é considerado dia útil. Já domingos e feriados não entram na contagem.

A regra está prevista no artigo 459 da CLT, que determina que o salário mensal deve ser pago, no máximo, até o quinto dia útil do mês seguinte ao trabalhado.

Quando é o quinto dia útil de outubro de 2026?

No cálculo do prazo para pagamento do salário, são considerados os dias de segunda-feira a sábado. Domingos e feriados ficam fora da contagem.

Primeiro dia útil: 1º de outubro (quinta-feira);

Segundo dia útil: 2 de outubro (sexta-feira);

Terceiro dia útil: 3 de outubro (sábado);

Quarto dia útil: 5 de outubro (segunda-feira);

Quinto dia útil: 6 de outubro (terça-feira).

Portanto, para quem trabalha com carteira assinada, o quinto dia útil de outubro de 2026 é 6 de outubro.

Sábado conta como dia útil para o pagamento do salário?

Sim. Para a contagem do prazo previsto na CLT para o pagamento de salários, o sábado é considerado dia útil.

A contagem é interrompida aos domingos e feriados. Por isso, mesmo que o trabalhador não tenha expediente aos sábados, o dia entra no cálculo do quinto dia útil.

Essa regra é específica para o prazo de pagamento do salário e não significa que o sábado seja necessariamente um dia normal de trabalho para todos os empregados.

Confira quando cai o quinto dia útil de outubro de 2026 e a data limite para o pagamento do salário. — Foto: Rafa Neddermeyer/Agência Brasil

O que acontece se o salário não for pago até o quinto dia útil?

O artigo 459 da CLT estabelece o prazo máximo para o pagamento do salário. Se o empregador não cumprir a data-limite, o trabalhador pode buscar orientação para cobrar os valores atrasados.

Em caso de atraso, o empregado pode recorrer à Justiça do Trabalho para cobrar o pagamento devido, com os acréscimos que forem aplicáveis. O sindicato da categoria também pode auxiliar na defesa dos direitos dos trabalhadores e na adoção das medidas cabíveis.

Atrasos frequentes ou prolongados no pagamento podem caracterizar descumprimento das obrigações do empregador.

Dependendo das circunstâncias e da gravidade da situação, isso pode levar ao reconhecimento da rescisão indireta, quando o trabalhador encerra o contrato por falta grave do empregador e pode ter direito às verbas de uma demissão sem justa causa.

O empregador também pode estar sujeito à fiscalização e às penalidades previstas na legislação trabalhista.

articles.title: Três pessoas são resgatadas após 70 dias à deriva no Oceano Pacífico | G1
articles.standfirst: Grupo desapareceu durante viagem entre duas ilhas e foi localizado por uma embarcação estrangeira.
articles.summary: Grupo desapareceu durante viagem entre duas ilhas e foi localizado por uma embarcação estrangeira.
articles.body:
Os três sobreviventes ficaram à deriva pelo Oceano Pacífico durante 70 dias antes de serem resgatados. — Foto: Reprodução/NBC Bougainville News

Um grupo de três pessoas foi encontrado na última segunda-feira (28) após passar 70 dias à deriva no Oceano Pacífico. Moradores de Bougainville, na Papua-Nova Guiné , na Oceania, eles viajavam cerca de 150 quilômetros entre duas ilhas do arquipélago quando a embarcação ficou sem combustível e acabaram percorrendo cerca de 4 mil quilômetros fora da rota.

Os dois homens e a mulher viajavam da ilha de Nissan para Buka quando desapareceram, em 18 de julho. Eles foram identificados como Mitchell Tokiapron, Darell Tokiapron e Horen Kapiatuon.

O barco em que estavam perdeu velocidade e potência durante o trajeto. O motor Yamaha de 60 cavalos ficou sem combustível, deixando a embarcação sem propulsão e à mercê das correntes marítimas.

A viagem, que deveria ligar duas ilhas da região de Bougainville, acabou levando o trio para uma área distante do trajeto original.

O trio foi localizado nesta segunda por uma embarcação estrangeira que navegava pelo Pacífico.

As buscas foram coordenadas pelo Governo Autônomo de Bougainville, em conjunto com o centro local de coordenação de resgates marítimos e o centro conjunto de coordenação de resgates.

Depois de serem encontrados, os três foram levados para o centro médico mais próximo, em Kiribati, onde receberam atendimento.

Até o momento, não havia informações detalhadas sobre o estado de saúde dos passageiros.

Distância entre as ilhas de Nissan e Buka, na Papua-Nova Guiné. — Foto: Reprodução/Google Maps

O caso do trio encontrado não foi o primeiro a acontecer na travessia entre ilhas de Papua-Nova Guiné.

Recentemente, oito homens, uma mulher e duas crianças fizeram o mesmo trajeto em uma embarcação de sete metros. O motor de popa apresentou uma falha, e o grupo ficou à deriva por mais de 19 horas.

Eles foram encontrados depois que a tripulação de um navio médico da Indonésia percebeu sinais de lanternas no mar.

Já em outro incidente, os passageiros não tiveram a mesma sorte.

Duas semanas antes do trio encontrado nesta semana desaparecerem, seis homens morreram afogados enquanto viajavam entre as ilhas de Muliama e Feni, na costa leste da província de New Ireland.

Na ocasião, uma embarcação com nove pessoas virou em meio ao mar agitado. Três passageiros conseguiram chegar à ilha de Tefa após passarem cerca de seis horas à deriva, enquanto os outros seis desapareceram e tiveram os corpos encontrados dias depois durante as buscas.

O primeiro foi localizado na costa da ilha de Djaul, a mais de 250 quilômetros do ponto onde os sobreviventes chegaram.

articles.title: Singapore plays matchmaker to public officers
articles.summary: Singapore’s governnment is playing cupid to public officers in their dating journey.
articles.body: Singapore’s governnment is playing cupid to public officers in their dating journey. With more Singaporeans marrying late or staying single, the government has launched a pilot called FirstDate for some public officers aged 21 to 35. The project aims to put an end to “swipe fatigue” associated with some dating apps and build “a thoughtful connection,” according to the website.To get a match, users have to sign in with the city’s digital identity system and complete a questionnaire about their interests, habits, values and preferences. Applications close Oct 5. The experiment comes as Singapore steps up efforts to reverse its record-low birth rate, a trend officials have called an existential challenge.Prime Minister Lawrence Wong put families at the centre of a key speech in Aug where he unveiled one of the world’s most generous attempts to get people to have more babies and make public housing more accessible.FirstDate started as an idea at the Government Technology Agency’s annual hackathon to explore the challenges people face when meeting someone new, according to the website. Government matchmaking isn’t new in Singapore. The Social Development Unit was set up in 1984 to encourage graduate singles to mingle at dinners, dances and overseas trips. The unit was formed as more university-educated women remained single, a trend which then-PM Lee Kuan Yew linked to concerns about the country’s future talent pool. SDU moved away from direct matchmaking in recent years with the rise of dating apps.Other countries struggling with low birth rates have tried similar measures. Tokyo’s metropolitan government launched a dating app in 2024. In South Korea, local governments have organised dating events and offered marriage incentives.You use AI every day. articles.summary: A 5.44-magnitude earthquake jolted Afghanistan’s Hindu Kush region early Thursday, according to the GFZ German Research Centre for Geosciences.
articles.body: A 5.44-magnitude earthquake jolted Afghanistan’s Hindu Kush region early Thursday, according to the GFZ German Research Centre for Geosciences.The earthquake struck at 0129 GMT (6.59 am IST), with its epicentre initially located at 36.05 degrees north latitude and 68.87 degrees east longitude. The quake occurred at a depth of 10 km, making it a relatively shallow earthquake.There were no immediate reports of casualties or damage.The Hindu Kush is one of the most seismically active regions around Afghanistan and Pakistan. Earthquakes in the broader Hindu Kush-Pamir region can occur at both shallow and great depths, with some linked to complex tectonic activity beneath the mountain ranges.The wider region lies within the zone of continuing collision between the Indian and Eurasian plates, which has produced frequent earthquakes across the Himalaya, Hindu Kush and surrounding mountain systems.The shallow depth of Thursday’s earthquake is notable because earthquakes occurring closer to the surface can produce stronger shaking near the epicentre than much deeper earthquakes of similar magnitude.The Hindu Kush region has experienced several earthquakes in recent years, including moderate and deeper events recorded by international and regional seismological agencies.You use AI every day. articles.title: Legal setback for Trump: Second judge halts $100,000 H-1B visa fee
articles.summary: A second US federal judge has blocked US President Donald Trump’s $100,000 fee on new H-1B visas for highly skilled foreign workers, dealing another legal
articles.body: A second US federal judge has blocked US President Donald Trump’s $100,000 fee on new H-1B visas for highly skilled foreign workers, dealing another legal setback to the administration’s attempt to sharply increase the cost of the programme.US district judge Haywood Gilliam in Oakland, California, ruled that US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) and the State Department failed to follow required rule-making procedures before putting the fee into effect.Gilliam granted a request from a coalition of unions, employers and nonprofit organisations that are challenging the fee in court. The ruling prevents the agencies from implementing the charge while that case proceeds.The plaintiffs argued that federal agencies could not introduce the fee without following the notice-and-comment procedures required under US administrative law.Gilliam agreed that the agencies had failed to follow those procedures before implementing the fee.The ruling comes after another federal judge in Boston separately blocked the fee in June in a case brought by 20 US states. That judge, US District Judge Leo Sorokin, concluded that the administration had exceeded its authority by imposing the charge without congressional approval.A Boston-based federal appeals court in July declined to put that ruling on hold, leaving the fee blocked in that case while the administration's appeal continues.Why did Trump impose the $100,000 fee?The H-1B programme allows US employers to hire foreign workers in specialty occupations that typically require specialised education or training.Congress created the programme in 1990. It provides 65,000 visas each year, with another 20,000 reserved for workers with advanced US degrees.H-1B visas are particularly important to technology companies, which rely on them to recruit specialised workers from countries including India and China. The visas generally allow workers to remain in the US for three to six years.Before Trump's fee was introduced, employers typically paid around $2,000 to $5,000 in government fees depending on the circumstances of the application.Trump introduced the fee as part of his broader immigration crackdown, arguing that companies had abused the H-1B programme by using foreign workers to replace Americans with cheaper labour.His administration has also introduced enhanced scrutiny of H-1B applicants and proposed changes to the visa selection process that would favour higher-skilled and higher-paid workers.The administration invoked presidential powers under federal immigration law to restrict the entry of foreign nationals whose admission it said could be detrimental to US interests.The $100,000 charge represented a dramatic increase over the programme's traditional fees.What happens to the fee now?Trump's original fee was due to expire on September 21, but the White House extended it for another year. The extension would keep the policy in place through September 2027, although the fee is currently blocked by court orders.Separately, the Department of Homeland Security has proposed a permanent fee of about $103,000. That proposal is being pursued through a formal rule-making process, meaning it raises different legal questions from the lawsuits challenging Trump's original $100,000 charge. The proposed fee is also likely to face legal challenges.The US Chamber of Commerce, the country's largest business lobbying group, has filed another lawsuit challenging the $100,000 fee. It is appealing after a judge rejected its claims that Trump lacked authority to impose the charge.Few employers have paid the $100,000 fee since it was introduced, according to Reuters.What does this mean for Indian H-1B applicants?The H-1B programme is particularly significant for Indian professionals because Indian nationals make up a large share of H-1B workers and technology companies are among the programme's biggest users.The original $100,000 fee does not apply to every H-1B worker. It was aimed at certain new H-1B applicants seeking to enter the US from abroad and did not apply to renewals of existing visas or to foreign nationals already in the US on student visas who transition to H-1B status.The current court rulings therefore do not amount to a cancellation of the H-1B programme. They concern the administration's attempt to impose the additional $100,000 charge.For employers and prospective workers, however, the competing court cases and the separate proposal for a roughly $103,000 permanent fee leave the future cost and rules surrounding new H-1B hiring uncertain.You use AI every day. articles.title: Pilot who 'never planned to fly': Mumbaikar Smit Machchhar's journey from textile course to saving 180 lives on flydubai flight
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Captain Smit Machchhar never grew up dreaming of flying planes.
articles.body: MUMBAI: Captain Smit Machchhar never grew up dreaming of flying planes. In fact, when he was 19, his career path appeared to be taking him in an entirely different direction — towards his family's textile business.An aviation seminar during a management course changed that.More than a decade later, the Mumbaikar found himself at the controls of a flydubai Boeing 737 MAX during one of the most terrifying moments of his flying career — after his co-pilot allegedly attacked him in the cockpit as the aircraft was carrying 174 passengers from Dubai to Tel Aviv.Despite being injured, Machchhar is reported to have fought back and helped prevent the aircraft from plunging further. The plane had dropped thousands of feet in a matter of seconds before passengers and crew intervened and the aircraft was eventually diverted to Saudi Arabia.Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu later identified Machchhar as the captain and praised his actions, saying he had helped prevent a major disaster.From textile engineering to cockpitMachchhar's journey into aviation was anything but conventional.In a podcast interview recorded around a year before the incident, he recalled that becoming a pilot was not a childhood ambition. After school, he initially enrolled in a textile engineering course because he expected to eventually contribute to his family's business.He later opted for a management course to prepare himself for the business.It was during that course, when he was just 19, that he attended an aviation seminar."Unlike a lot of other aviators right now, aviation was not like a childhood dream," Machchhar said in the interview.The seminar changed his plans.His decision to enter aviation initially worried his mother."My mom was scared," he recalled, explaining that commercial aviation was far less familiar to people around him 15-17 years ago. His father, however, was more comfortable with his decision.Machchhar subsequently completed his commercial pilot training in New Zealand before obtaining his Boeing 737 type rating at the Flight Safety Training Centre (FSTC) in Manesar, Gurgaon.From SpiceJet to flydubaiMachchhar joined SpiceJet in 2011 and spent more than a decade with the airline, eventually becoming a senior commander and Line Training Captain.According to his professional profile, he accumulated more than 9,500 flying hours with SpiceJet, including over 6,400 hours as pilot-in-command. As a Line Training Captain, he was responsible for training, assessing and mentoring other pilots while ensuring adherence to operational and safety procedures.He moved to flydubai in June 2022 as a direct-entry captain and has since been flying the Boeing 737 fleet.His profile lists more than 9,750 hours of flying experience and experience on the Boeing 737-800 and Boeing 737 MAX 8/9.A senior pilot who had trained Machchhar previously described him as a "very decent and sober person" who was always willing to learn.Machchhar's brother is also a pilot with flydubai.The flight that plunged thousands of feetThe flydubai flight was carrying 174 passengers, including 166 Israeli citizens, when the incident unfolded.According to flight-tracking data, the Boeing 737 MAX descended from roughly 30,875 feet to 16,750 feet in just 29 seconds. Flightradar24 recorded an extreme descent rate of around 30,000 feet per minute.Reports said the Omani co-pilot attacked Machchhar with a knife. The captain was injured but managed to resist while the aircraft was in danger of losing control.Passengers and crew eventually entered the cockpit and subdued the attacker.The aircraft was then diverted and landed at Tabuk in Saudi Arabia. Two additional pilots who had been travelling as passengers were also on board and later took over the aircraft.The severity of the descent surprised aviation experts. Former United Airlines pilot and aviation safety expert Steve Arroyo said he was surprised the aircraft remained intact after the extreme manoeuvre, while aviation investigator Jeff Guzzetti said the aircraft had enough altitude left for the pilots to recover.The aircraft also reportedly suffered damage to its rudder during the descent.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: UK property tycoon left £100m estate; daughter was named 80%, but his son challenged his will, and the High Court later upheld an earlier version
articles.summary: Kevin Patrick Reeves, also known as Kevin Patrick Frain, built a fortune estimated at up to £100 million from property and other investments before his
articles.body: Kevin Patrick Reeves, also known as Kevin Patrick Frain, built a fortune estimated at up to £100 million from property and other investments before his death in February 2019, aged 71. His estate later became the centre of a dispute between his children and grandchildren over which of two wills reflected his wishes. A 2014 will left 80% of the residuary estate to his youngest daughter, Louise Reeves, while her half-sister Lisa received the remaining 20%. Reeves’ son Simon, known as Bill, challenged the document and sought to have an earlier 2012 will recognised instead. The case eventually reached the England and Wales High Court (King's Bench Division).Kevin Patrick Reeves’ 2014 will dramatically changed the inheritanceThe 2014 will represented a major change from the arrangement set out in Kevin Reeves’ earlier testament. Under the 2014 document, Louise Reeves received 80% of the residuary estate, alongside a specific property and her father’s Rolls-Royce Phantom. Her half-sister Lisa Murray received the remaining 20% of the residuary estate and another specific property. Reeves’ son Bill was left only certain personal possessions, while his grandchildren Ryan and Ria were excluded from the later will. The earlier 2012 will had instead divided 80% of the estate equally between Louise, Lisa and Bill, with the remaining 20% divided equally between Ryan and Ria.Bill challenged whether his father understood the willBill opposed the 2014 will, arguing that his father had not known or approved its contents and, alternatively, that it had been procured through undue influence by Louise. The High Court heard evidence during a three-week trial, with the judgment recording testimony from 49 witnesses. A central issue was Reeves’ ability to understand the document he signed. The court considered his limited literacy alongside his considerable business experience and the substantial change between the 2012 and 2014 wills. The challenge was therefore not simply about whether the distribution appeared unequal, but whether the later document represented Reeves’ properly understood testamentary intentions.The High Court rejected the 2014 willIn 2022, the High Court ruled in favour of the earlier 2012 will rather than the 2014 document. The court did not uphold the allegation that Louise had exercised undue influence over her father. Instead, the 2014 will was rejected because the evidence did not establish that Reeves knew and approved its contents. The earlier will consequently governed the distribution of the estate. Under that document, Louise, Lisa and Bill were each entitled to an equal share of 80% of the residuary estate, while Ryan and Ria shared the remaining 20%. The outcome meant the 80% provision in Louise’s favour under the later will did not stand.The 2025 case concerned the legal costs of the disputeThe case returned to the High Court in 2025, but this time the issue was costs rather than which will was valid. In Reeves v Frain & McKinnon, Mr Justice Dexter Dias considered an appeal concerning the costs of the earlier litigation. Simon Frain and Mark Ryan McKinnon had challenged an earlier costs decision involving damages-based agreements used by their solicitors. The 2025 judgment upheld the relevant ruling that those agreements could not support recovery of the solicitors’ fees in the way claimed.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.body: NEW DELHI: A special National Investigation Agency (NIA) court has directed that charges be framed against separatist Yasin Malik and six other accused under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) for allegedly receiving foreign funding from the Pakistani establishment through hawala channels.The other accused are Zahoor Ahmed Shah Watali, Abdul Rashid Sheikh, Shabir Ahmad Shah, Naval Kishore Kapoor, Trison Farms and Construction Pvt Ltd, and Masarat Alam Bhat.Special NIA Judge Prashant Sharma ordered that charges be framed after considering the material against the accused."I conclude that prima facie, there is sufficient material on record based upon which strong suspicion is raised against all seven accused persons, namely Zahoor Ahmad Shah Watali, Naval Kishore Kapoor, M/s Trison Farms and Constructions Pvt Ltd, Mohd. Yasin Malik, Shabir Ahmad Shah, Masarat Alam and Abdul Rashid Sheikh, for which said accused persons have to be charged with offence u/sec. 3 of PMLA, punishable u/sec. 4 of PMLA," the Special Judge ordered on Wednesday.The investigation conducted by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) found that the scheduled offences generated proceeds of crime amounting to Rs. 8,94,87,639, which were allegedly received, routed, transferred, concealed, possessed, acquired and/or used by the accused through various channels.The court noted that, according to the NIA's second supplementary chargesheet, Malik received Rs. 15,75,595 from Saudi Arabia. It said Malik received foreign funds totalling Rs. 30,75,595 as alleged proceeds of crime.The ED case is based on an NIA case registered in 2017.The agency alleged that Malik, then head of the Jammu & Kashmir Liberation Front (JKLF), received foreign funds through Zahoor Ahmad Shah Watali, along with Shabir Ahmad Shah and Masarat Alam, during 2015-16.According to the ED, emails linked to Malik showed that he had established a network to raise funds abroad, which were used to support the JKLF and carry out secessionist activities and violence in Jammu and Kashmir.The ED also alleged that the money was routed through cash couriers who collected funds from the Pakistan High Commission in New Delhi and delivered them to Hurriyat leaders, including Malik.(With ANI inputs)Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: In 2024, Texas biologists turned more than 160 donated Christmas trees into an underwater reef at Granger Lake, where fish can use them as habitat within 15 minutes
articles.summary: The Christmas season is around the corner, and the must-have Christmas tree often ends up on the curb once the holidays are over, needles trailing down
articles.body: The Christmas season is around the corner, and the must-have Christmas tree often ends up on the curb once the holidays are over, needles trailing down the driveway. They rarely get a second act. In 2024, more than 160 of them got a second act. None of them were headed for a living room, but a lake. The Christmas trees were dropped off at Yeti's flagship store in Austin. Biologists and technicians from the Texas Parks and Wildlife Department (TPWD) Inland Fisheries Division hauled the trees to Granger Lake and sank them as a single large reef. The project also involved the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers and had a specific purpose: to give the fish somewhere to be!From Austin to the lakeThe logistics were simple. Yeti collected the Christmas trees at the store. TPWD crews moved them to the water. The Army Corps was part of the partnership that made the installation possible. All this was to improve fish habitat at Granger Lake.“This project not only enhanced fish habitat at Granger Lake, but it helped grow public awareness of the need and benefits to fish and anglers from restoring and enhancing fish habitat in Texas lakes. We are incredibly thankful to our partners at Yeti and the Army Corps of Engineers, as well as the dozens of other partner organisations and volunteers who collaborate with our biologists to deliver over 50 habitat restoration or enhancement projects each year in Texas rivers and lakes,” Tim Birdsong, TPWD Inland Fisheries Division Director, said in a release.Granger has a reputation for crappie. What it lacks, according to Patrick Ireland, the TPWD district supervisor for San Marcos and Austin, is natural fish habitat. And that’s exactly where the Christmas trees have a part to play. These trees can help the fish and the people chasing them.All this depends on how a Christmas tree behaves underwater. Recycled Christmas trees are often used as fish attractors because the small spaces between the limbs provide cover for small prey fish. Where prey gathers, bigger sport fish like largemouth bass and crappie follow. Anglers know this, and that’s why fish attractor locations double as a map to where fish are concentrated.Reservoirs also carry a slower problem. As they age, the submerged timber that once gave fish cover decomposes, and the habitat goes with it.“The trees were installed as part of a large reef that will serve as habitat for fish in Granger Lake in the coming years and as an area for anglers to target. Granger is known for crappie and this reef should benefit both the anglers and the fish at this lake, which otherwise has limited natural fish habitat,” Patrick Ireland said.The fir trees sitting in the water can provide immediate habitat for fish, which they can use almost immediately, in about 15 minutes. Trees are also a natural product that breaks down over up to two years, providing benefits to the ecosystem as they decompose, including food for periphyton and invertebrates that in turn feed fish. The depth of the tree and water temperature are some factors that determine the duration before the breakdown occurs. So the reef works twice. First as shelter, then as a slow meal.“TPWD Inland Fisheries has worked for many years to improve habitat in reservoirs across Texas. As reservoirs age, submerged aquatic habitat tends to degrade over the years as submerged timber decomposes. The installation of natural brush, such as Christmas trees, can help mitigate this decline in aquatic habitat,” Patrick Ireland added.And just like that, Phoebe’s (Buffay) wish was granted. The trees that had no purpose after Christmas got one even after the festive season. They didn’t end up in the shredder. Instead, they became shelter, food and habitat for fish at Granger Lake.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani has a plan for the hottest station in the city's subway, the one he calls a 'chamber of horrors,' and it isn't AC, it is...
articles.summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani wants to put the heat that makes the city's subway unbearable every summer to work.
articles.body: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani wants to put the heat that makes the city's subway unbearable every summer to work. The city, New York Governor Kathy Hochul and the Metropolitan Transportation Authority (MTA) have announced a study into a thermal energy network (TEN) at the Brooklyn Bridge-City Hall and Chambers Street station complex in Lower Manhattan. The plan is to pull heat off the platforms in summer, store it deep underground, and use it to warm nearby city buildings in winter.The $800,000 feasibility study is funded by the New York State Energy Research and Development Authority. If the system is built, it would be the first thermal energy network in any US transit system. Mamdani made the announcement from a steamy platform inside the complex, which he called a "chamber of horrors". Brooklyn Bridge-City Hall averaged 96°F (about 35.5°C) through summer 2025, making it one of the hottest stations in New York.Subway heat would be stored 600 feet below Chambers Street stationRadiant cooling panels would absorb heat from the Brooklyn Bridge-City Hall platforms, which serve the 4, 5 and 6 lines, and possibly from the Chambers Street J/Z platforms too. These panels circulate chilled water through walls, ceilings or floors, so the cool surfaces soak up heat directly. Officials say this can be 25 to 35% more energy-efficient than traditional air conditioning.The captured heat would travel through pipes to geothermal boreholes drilled 500 to 600 feet beneath an abandoned centre platform at Chambers Street. Since nobody uses that platform, the MTA can test the system without disturbing the more than 18,000 riders who pass through the station on an average weekday.City Hall could be heated with waste heat from the New York subwayIn winter, the stored heat would be piped to City Hall, the David N. Dinkins Municipal Building, Tweed Courthouse and Surrogate's Court. Mamdani said heating the Municipal Building alone costs the city about $1.4 million (roughly Rs 12 crore) a year.The same technology already runs at St Patrick's Cathedral and the New York Botanical Garden, besides several hospitals and universities. A subway station is a tougher job. "Bringing down the temperature is a real challenge in a century-old system with open entrances and vents everywhere," MTA chair and CEO Janno Lieber said.Part of the problem comes from the trains themselves. Air-conditioned cars vent their hot air into stations and tunnels. At Brooklyn Bridge-City Hall, trains waiting at the 6 line terminal add even more heat. Mamdani said some stations get up to 20 degrees hotter than the street above, adding that commuting in his wool suit is "far from a therapeutic experience".Mamdani's subway cooling plan now depends on what lies beneath Chambers StreetThe contract for the feasibility study is expected to be awarded this fall. If the ground beneath Chambers Street proves suitable, design work would begin in early 2027.The study runs alongside a separate renovation of the Chambers Street station, which opened in 1913 and has long been one of the most neglected stops in the system. That project, paid for through congestion pricing, will fix leaks, replace tiles and mosaics, and upgrade stairways and lighting.Not every rider is convinced the money is well spent, and the MTA still says the quickest relief is getting people onto air-conditioned trains faster. Lieber kept his own expectations modest. Bringing the platforms down by even a few degrees, he said, would be "the difference between total misery and merely sweltering".You use AI every day. articles.title: Rape case rocks Cornell: New transcript reveals victim informed police; fresh spotlight on DA’s decision not to charge
articles.summary: A newly surfaced transcript of a Cornell University student's interview with campus police is raising fresh questions about why criminal charges were not
articles.body: A newly surfaced transcript of a Cornell University student's interview with campus police is raising fresh questions about why criminal charges were not filed after she alleged she was sexually assaulted by fraternity members in 2024.The woman, who is referred to with the placeholder Jane Doe in a civil lawsuit, told Cornell University police during a two-day interview in November 2024 that she could say with “100% confidence” that she was raped, according to a transcript obtained by CBS News.The transcript also records her saying she was “completely and totally incapacitated” and describing sexual encounters that she said became coercive after she had consumed alcohol and drugs.But Tompkins County district attorney Matthew Van Houten has said he never saw the transcript before his office decided not to bring charges.The revelation has added a new layer to the controversy surrounding the case, which was reopened this week after Doe filed a civil lawsuit against Cornell University and seven Chi Phi fraternity members. Van Houten has said he is now reviewing the new information and could present the case to a grand jury.Details of transcriptThe interview took place on November 14 and 15, 2024, more than three weeks after the alleged assault at the Chi Phi fraternity house.According to the transcript, Doe told investigators that the night began with consensual sexual activity but later changed as more men became involved. She said she had consumed alcohol and ketamine and had gaps in her memory.At one point, she described being physically hit and said she had pushed away unwanted touching. She also told investigators that she had said she was uncomfortable, that she was tired and, on some occasions, no.When investigators asked whether she eventually gave in after becoming exhausted from dealing with the men, she responded: “Yes. It was coercion.”When asked about the later part of the night, she said: “I can say with 100% confidence I was raped.”She also said she did not remember the end of the night and did not know how many people had sex with her while she was in that state.Van Houten has said his office's original decision was based on a six-page sworn statement that did not, in his view, describe conduct meeting New York's criminal definition of rape.He told CBS News that he had never seen the longer transcript containing Doe's explicit statement that she was raped.“I'm going to follow up on this because this is news to me,” Van Houten said, according to CBS.He said the transcript could change the picture his office had when it initially decided not to prosecute and that he would obtain it from Cornell police.Cornell University Police, however, said the department had shared “all investigatory information” with the DA's office in 2024, according to CBS. It was not immediately clear whether that material included the interview transcript.Doe's lawyer has questioned why prosecutors did not investigate further, pointing to her account as well as messages allegedly exchanged by fraternity members about the encounter. The defendants have not been convicted, and lawyers for some of them have denied the allegations.What is the ‘voluntary intoxication loophole’?The case has also reignited debate over New York's treatment of sexual assault involving voluntarily intoxicated victims.Under current state law, prosecutors generally must establish circumstances such as physical force, forcible compulsion, unconsciousness or mental incapacitation caused by drugs or intoxicants administered without the victim's knowledge or consent.That means prosecutors can face an additional legal hurdle when a person voluntarily consumes alcohol or drugs and later becomes so intoxicated that they are unable to consent.Victim advocates have dubbed this the “voluntary intoxication loophole”. They argue that a person's inability to consent should not depend on whether they voluntarily consumed the substance that caused their incapacitation.Van Houten has defended his earlier decision by pointing to those legal limits, saying prosecutors are required to apply the law as it exists rather than make a determination based on the moral seriousness of the allegations.The Cornell case has renewed calls in Albany to change the law.Assemblyman Jeffrey Dinowitz, who has sponsored legislation aimed at addressing voluntary intoxication in sexual assault cases since 2019, said the Cornell allegations were the kind of case his proposed changes were intended to address.New York is among a group of states whose laws have historically made a distinction between voluntary and involuntary intoxication when determining whether a victim was mentally incapacitated.Other states have already changed their laws. Minnesota revised its law in 2021 after its Supreme Court overturned a sexual misconduct conviction involving a voluntarily intoxicated victim. Michigan made a similar change in 2023, while Texas followed in 2025.What happened at Cornell in 2024?Doe's civil lawsuit alleges that she was pressured to consume ketamine, marijuana and alcohol at the Chi Phi house on October 19-20, 2024, before becoming incapacitated and being sexually assaulted by multiple fraternity members.The lawsuit also includes alleged messages from a fraternity group chat referring to the woman and inviting other members into the room.Cornell conducted its own investigation, which resulted in disciplinary action against members of the fraternity, including suspensions and expulsions. The Chi Phi chapter was subsequently closed.The criminal investigation, however, initially ended without charges.Van Houten has now reopened the investigation following the civil lawsuit and the emergence of additional allegations and evidence.The DA has said he will review the newly surfaced transcript and other material and could take the case before a grand jury.The transcript has also intensified scrutiny of the handoff between Cornell police and the district attorney's office, after the DA said he had not previously seen the interview in which Doe explicitly told investigators she believed she had been raped.You use AI every day.
